get_diagram.description: Read the active diagram ID, revision, name, save status, selection, viewport, and simplified elements including group IDs, original text, rendered labels, and line geometry. Coordinates are scene units and angles are radians. Call before editing; the browser must remain connected.

apply_operations.description: Atomically create, edit, organize, or delete canvas elements. Each operation is a flat object with an op field (not type). Basic example: {"op":"create_shape","id":"box-1","shape":"rectangle","x":100,"y":100}. create_shape accepts only rectangle, ellipse or diamond. For imported library shapes, call list_custom_shapes then the dedicated insert_custom_shape tool, or include {"op":"insert_custom_shape","shapeId":"ID_FROM_LIST","idPrefix":"copy-1","x":100,"y":100} in this batch. Read get_diagram first and pass its diagramId and expectedRevision. A batch is one native undo step, validates fully before changing the canvas, and saves in IndexedDB. Use requestId for safe retries; reuse it only with identical arguments. Text, resize, rotation, styling, straight/elbow connectors, groups, alignment, and duplication are supported. Locked elements and unsupported edits fail without changing the scene. Preview afterward to inspect layout. If saving fails, the canvas edit still succeeded: saveStatus is error and saveError explains why. Export a backup or retry saving before reloading; retry receipts become durable only when the scene saves. Geometry edits recalculate attached elbow routes.

oneOf.description: Create a basic rectangle, ellipse or diamond, not an imported library shape. For custom shapes, use list_custom_shapes and insert_custom_shape. Angles are radians. Labels wrap; containers can grow to fit text.
Create standalone text. Optional width enables wrapping.
Create an unbound line or arrow (kind defaults to line). Arrowheads require kind arrow.

points.description: Absolute scene coordinates. Replaces line geometry; arrow bindings are preserved unless explicitly changed.

oneOf.description: Connect two basic shapes with a bound straight or elbow arrow, optionally with a label.
Move an element, its label, and attached connectors. Use translate for a group of elements.
Edit geometry, text/label, and styling. Set text to empty to remove a label. Text height is measured automatically. Set fromId/toId to null to detach an arrow end. Elbow arrows cannot be rotated.

points.description: Absolute scene coordinates. Replaces line geometry; arrow bindings are preserved unless explicitly changed.

oneOf.description: Delete selected elements, their labels, and incident arrows. One undo restores all of them.

Duplicate elements, labels, and arrows connecting selected shapes. Defaults to offset 40,40. New IDs use idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, etc. Returns source-to-copy mappings. External bindings are detached; groups are copied with new IDs.
Group elements and labels using a fresh groupId. Include all members of existing groups to nest them.
Remove specified group memberships, preserving any other nested groups.
Move multiple elements by the same offset. Labels move with containers; attached arrows update once.
Align individual elements by their rotated bounding boxes. Labels move with their containers.
Evenly space individual elements with equal gaps while preserving the two outer edges. Fails if the available span cannot fit them.

Insert a copy of an installed custom shape at x/y (top-left of its bounds), preserving size, styles, groups and internal bindings. Creates IDs idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, etc.; returns their sourceId/id mappings in copies. The installed template is unchanged.

shapeId.description: Exact installed template ID returned by list_custom_shapes; not a shape name or native type.

idPrefix.description: Unique prefix for new element IDs (idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, etc.). Use a different prefix for each new copy.

requestId.description: Use a fresh UUID per batch. Retry with identical arguments and the same ID. The last 128 successful IDs per diagram are saved atomically with the scene and survive reloads. Replays return current state plus appliedRevision without repeating edits, even after undo. Reusing an ID with different arguments fails.

list_diagrams.description: List the saved browser library and active diagram ID/revision, plus saveStatus and saveError if current canvas edits could not be saved. Listing still works after a save failure so trash can be cleared to free space. Each diagram includes storageSize estimates in bytes: sceneBytes (including embedded images), recoveryBytes (previous save), and metadataBytes. Sum these for its estimated saved data size; browser database overhead is excluded. Include trash to find diagrams for restoration or permanent deletion and account for their storage.

create_diagram.description: Create and save an empty diagram. Returns its stable ID and revision. Does not change the active canvas; use open_diagram explicitly.

open_diagram.description: Open a saved diagram in the browser after saving current edits. Read list_diagrams first and pass its active ID/revision to avoid switching away from a newer human edit. Switching resets the editor undo history.

manage_diagram.description: Rename, duplicate, move to trash, restore from trash, or recover the previous saved version. Requires the target revision from list_diagrams/get_diagram. Trash is recoverable. Duplicate creates a new ID without opening it. Recover replaces contents and clears undo if active.

delete_diagrams.description: Permanently delete one or more trashed diagrams, including their embedded images, metadata and recovery copies. This cannot be undone. First call list_diagrams with includeTrash:true and pass the IDs and revisions of the trashed diagrams to remove. To empty trash, include every trashed diagram from that list. The entire batch is atomic: missing, restored or changed diagrams fail without removing anything. Active and untrashed diagrams cannot be deleted. Works even if the active canvas cannot save; leaves its edits untouched. Returns deletedIds and count. After a timeout, inspect the library before retrying.

export_diagram.description: Export a saved or active diagram as editable excalidraw JSON, SVG, or PNG. Returns filename, mimeType, encoding (utf8/base64), sizeBytes, revision, artifactId, first data chunk and nextOffset. Read remaining chunks using read_export, concatenate data, then decode base64 for PNG. Artifacts expire after 5 minutes and stay only in browser memory. Export also works for an unsaved active canvas.

export_library.description: Back up the browser diagram library as versioned JSON, including trash by default. Returns a UTF-8 export artifact and first chunk; use read_export until nextOffset is null. Maximum backup is 100 diagrams / 64 MB. Diagrams are never saved on the server.

read_export.description: Read an export artifact chunk by artifactId and nextOffset. Concatenate chunks in order. Offsets are UTF-16 string offsets returned by the tool, not byte positions. Artifacts expire 5 minutes after creation.

begin_import.description: Begin a chunked editable diagram or library JSON upload, held in browser memory for 5 minutes. Returns uploadId and chunkSize. Append using write_import_chunk, then call import_diagram or import_library with uploadId. Use this for data larger than 256 KB. Call release_transfer to cancel an unfinished upload.

write_import_chunk.description: Append UTF-8 JSON text to an upload. Supply the exact nextOffset from the last response (0 initially). Chunks must be at most 64000 UTF-8 bytes and keep Unicode characters intact. Uploading alone does not modify saved diagrams.

import_diagram.description: Import editable .excalidraw JSON (16 MB maximum). Provide data directly for small files or an uploadId from begin_import/write_import_chunk. Default creates a new diagram and leaves the canvas active. Explicit replacement requires replaceDiagramId and expectedRevision; the previous saved contents remain recoverable. Files are fully validated before writing. Returns diagram metadata; use open_diagram to view a new import.

import_library.description: Restore a version 1 diagrams-library JSON backup (up to 100 diagrams / 64 MB). Provide data or uploadId. Imports all entries atomically with new diagram IDs, preserving names, scenes, images and trash state. Existing diagrams are never overwritten. Returns source-to-new ID mappings. Does not change the active canvas.

release_transfer.description: Release an export artifact or cancel an unfinished import to free browser memory. Safe to repeat. Use after saving an export locally.

preview_diagram.description: Render the active diagram, specified elements, or current selection as an MCP image for visual inspection. Includes labels, metadata, bounds, and the captured revision. Does not change the diagram or viewport. Images are rendered in the browser, bounded in size, and never stored on the server.

selectionOnly.description: Use the current human selection instead of the whole diagram. Mutually exclusive with elementIds.

fit_canvas.description: Fit the canvas to all elements, specified elementIds, or the current selection. Changes only the viewport; does not create an undo step or change diagram revision. Refuses while the user is editing.

selectionOnly.description: Use the current human selection instead of the whole diagram. Mutually exclusive with elementIds.

list_custom_shapes.description: Discover reusable custom shapes installed in the connected browser, including shapes from imported Excalidraw libraries. Returns IDs, optional imported names, text labels, element types, counts, and dimensions. Search by name, text, ID, or element type; use no query to browse unlabeled icons. Use preview_custom_shapes to see a numbered gallery before inserting anything, especially when names and text are absent. Pass a returned id as shapeId to insert_custom_shape, along with diagramId and expectedRevision from get_diagram, a unique idPrefix, and x/y coordinates. Do not use create_shape for library shapes: it only supports rectangle, ellipse and diamond. Use preview_diagram afterward to inspect the result. These templates are separate from saved diagrams. Use these IDs only with tools on this same MCP server/browser connection.

insert_custom_shape.description: Place a copy of an imported custom shape in the active diagram. First call list_custom_shapes to discover installed templates and use the exact returned id as shapeId. Use preview_custom_shapes to identify unlabeled icons before inserting. Call get_diagram for diagramId and expectedRevision. Pass flat arguments: diagramId, expectedRevision, shapeId, idPrefix, x, y, and optionally requestId. x/y position the top-left of the copy; original size, styling, groups and internal connections are preserved. Use a unique idPrefix for each copy. Returns new sourceId/id mappings in copies. The installed template is unchanged. This is one undo step and uses the same saving and retry behavior as apply_operations. Multiple shapes can also be inserted atomically using apply_operations with op: insert_custom_shape. Preview afterward to inspect layout.

requestId.description: Use a fresh UUID per batch. Retry with identical arguments and the same ID. The last 128 successful IDs per diagram are saved atomically with the scene and survive reloads. Replays return current state plus appliedRevision without repeating edits, even after undo. Reusing an ID with different arguments fails.

shapeId.description: Exact installed template ID returned by list_custom_shapes; not a shape name or native type.

idPrefix.description: Unique prefix for new element IDs (idPrefix-1, idPrefix-2, etc.). Use a different prefix for each new copy.

preview_custom_shapes.description: Inspect installed custom shapes visually before inserting them. Returns an MCP image showing a numbered gallery and metadata mapping each number to its shape ID, optional imported name, text, and dimensions. With no arguments, previews the first 12 shapes. Browse with query (name, text, ID, type), offset and limit (up to 16); nextOffset identifies the next page. Or provide shapeIds (up to 16) to preview specific templates in that order; one ID gives a larger detail view. shapeIds cannot be combined with query, offset or limit. Use the returned IDs with insert_custom_shape on this same MCP server/browser connection. This tool renders in browser memory without changing the active diagram, selection, viewport, undo history or installed templates. No images are stored on the server.

shapeIds.description: Exact IDs from list_custom_shapes. Preserves requested order; mutually exclusive with query, offset and limit.

query.description: Search optional imported names, text labels, IDs and element types; omit to browse unnamed shapes.
